item.title: Ethan Mollick：Much of the world is based on the assumption that the future is like the pas…
item.description:
Much of the world is based on the assumption that the future is like the past and an original meaning of “singularity” was a point where that relationship breaks. I don’t know if there will be one big Singularity, but a million little singularities across fields seems inevitable.

item.title: Ethan Mollick：After a brief but institution-eroding slop science era, it increasingly look…
item.description:
After a brief but institution-eroding slop science era, it increasingly looks like we are going to have two revolutions from AI:
1) Everything ever published will be re-read and re-judged in ways that human scientists never anticipated
2) Novel discoveries will start to come fast

item.title: Ethan Mollick：Just a reminder to the AI Labs that you should confirm that the models you a…
item.description:
Just a reminder to the AI Labs that you should confirm that the models you are shipping understand your products & how to use them (& update when you release new features). Nothing weirder than having your AI know everything about how to use your computer except for its own app.

item.title: Ethan Mollick：And I also think the positive use cases (like the evidence shows current AIs…
item.description:
And I also think the positive use cases (like the evidence shows current AIs provide good health information & financial advice & lead to startups etc.) are also undermeasured and underdiscussed.

We do need to worry about many dangers, but its worth building on successes as well

item.title: Ethan Mollick：I think most people who have been closely watching AI for the past few years…
item.description:
I think most people who have been closely watching AI for the past few years are likely surprised by how relatively rare terrible AI incidents have been, given a billion users overall and hundreds of millions of corporate users. Doesn’t mean that will continue, but surprising.

item.title: Ethan Mollick：When people talk about AI easily replacing workers, I think about this ethno…
item.description:
When people talk about AI easily replacing workers, I think about this ethnography of copier repair technicians in the 1990s.

You see how work is complicated and improvised by workers and informal and badly documented.

(But eventually technology did largely eliminate this job) https://t.co/DHGW060pUK

item.title: Ethan Mollick：Subtle problem with AI-written academic papers is that AI isn't calibrated f…
item.description:
Subtle problem with AI-written academic papers is that AI isn't calibrated for feedback. AI often just folds, but if you are sending a paper for review, challenges from peer reviewers should result in some attempt to defend your idea (while still giving up on it if really wrong)

item.description:
So much reporting on the Claude or OpenAI usage of the same handful of technology companies with competing products & huge cloud infrastructure of their own.

There are many, many more firms out there that are not direct competitors & whose use trends would be more informative.

item.description:
I will block replybots whose prompts make them generate inane comments connecting the poem to business process re-engineering or whatever, or those that quote a random line from the poem as "the part that people miss" etc. You can do better.

item.title: Ethan Mollick：How do you picture a superintelligence (if true superintelligence could ever…
item.description:
How do you picture a superintelligence (if true superintelligence could ever be real)? I like a trick from Dungeons and Dragons for running villains with 25 Intelligence: don't try to out-plan the players. Instead, whatever they do or roll, play it like the big bad saw it coming.

item.description:
They can use the channels built for humans, but which have far too much friction for any human to use. Your Clawlike is happy to navigate a phone tree or stay on hold or have an awkward conversation with an agent where they get rejected... and then try again.

item.description:
Every firm's customer service agents are about to be overwhelmed with Dots & Muses & etc. negotiating for better deals using voice/chat. Stories of people delegating this sort of work to their agents & saving money as a result are popping up and are going to only go more viral.

Every one of the apps from the AI Labs have weird edges and are underdocumented and break sometimes and update without any sort of notice or changelog and change UIs on a dime...

A broken early version of whatever product they are shipping is still better then what a well-built traditional product a lot of the time because LLMs are just unreasonably effective tools at doing a vast array of stuff and people & companies are learning to just roll with it.

item.description:
It does feel like every year OpenAI releases a variation on the same third-party ecosystem only to semi-abandon it: Plugins in 2023, GPTs and the GPT Store in 2023-2024, Apps in 2025, and now Plugins (same name, different thing than before) in 2026.

item.title: emollick：It also has a natural analog on teams as a persistent entity with a job that you …
item.description:
It also has a natural analog on teams as a persistent entity with a job that you can delegate to using existing team communication tools like Slack. I expect more Clawlikes soon, though I don’t think they are the final form of this type of AI.

item.title: emollick：I only used Dots briefly before launch, so can’t offer a detailed review, but I f…
item.description:
I only used Dots briefly before launch, so can’t offer a detailed review, but I found it to be good & very much in the rapidly-expanding Clawlike category with Muse & Grokbot. Using a capable model with access to your data as an assistant & second opinion is remarkably useful.

item.title: emollick：As least year's DevDay, this is what OpenAI said agents would look like. This is …
item.description:
As least year's DevDay, this is what OpenAI said agents would look like. This is before OpenClaw & self-organizing swarms, so this entire approach was scraped soon after:
1) AI is evolving quite quickly
2) The AI labs aren't always anticipating how fast in the products they make https://t.co/WQPZ7BVeli

item.title: emollick：The impact of AI on jobs is still pretty unclear at this point. I don't find this…
item.description:
The impact of AI on jobs is still pretty unclear at this point. I don't find this very surprising, as employers are still figuring out individual adoption, let alone how you use AI in complex organizations. Things may start to happen faster as agents capable of real work spread.

原文

item.title: emollick：In a world where cloud-based Clawlike assistants that give powerful models virtua…
item.description:
In a world where cloud-based Clawlike assistants that give powerful models virtual computers are increasingly looking like the way forward for personal AI, it really does seem to suggest the choices Apple made for Siri (on-device, limited capabilities) may be the wrong direction.
